title: Observability Handoff Checklist and Dashboard Compact Kit
content:
Purpose:
Compact, portable checklist and dashboard kit for engineering teams handing off a model or feature to oncall/ops. Focus is on the minimum telemetry and dashboards needed to investigate regressions during first 72 hours of a rollout and for routine handoffs between teams.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: feature owner, model owner, release engineer, SRE oncall
- Scope: token-serving paths, KV cache behavior, routing fallbacks, canary/rollout observability signals

Handoff checklist (must be completed before canary):
1) Metric provenance doc: single-line mapping from product event -> service metric -> dashboard widget. Attach the short mapping to the release ticket. Example:
   - user:generate -> inference.request.count -> "requests by route (1m rollup)"
   - user:generate.first_token -> inference.latency.p50_first_token -> "first-token latency by model"
2) Critical SLIs and ownership: define 3 SLIs with owners (name + pager):
   - SLI-1: First-token P50/P95 (model-owner)
   - SLI-2: Token emission error rate (engineer-oncall)
   - SLI-3: Cold-KV cache miss rate > threshold (infra/SRE)
3) Trace anchors: list of span names/tags to collect (add to trace sampling rules):
   - span: request.received (tags: route, tenant_id, model_version)
   - span: model.encode_inputs (tags: seq_len, batching_key)
   - span: runtime.kv_lookup (tags: kv_hit, kv_latency_ms)
   - span: runtime.generate_block (tags: token_count, quantized)
4) Dashboard compact kit (3 screens):
   - Overall health screen (single-row): total requests 1m, first-token P50/P95, errors per minute, deployment version, traffic % to canary
   - KV/caching screen: kv_hit_rate (1m), kv_miss_latency_p95, per-tenant cold_warm_index, eviction_count
   - Investigate-playlist screen: top 10 slow traces, slow token paths (long tail tokens), examples of recent user prompts for replay (anonymized)
5) Alert definitions to enable for canary:
   - Alert A: First-token P95 > 2x baseline for 10m -> severity P1 (notify model-owner + oncall)
   - Alert B: Error rate spike > 0.5% absolute for 5m -> P1 (engineer-oncall)
   - Alert C: KV miss rate increase > 15% baseline -> P2 (infra)
6) Synthetic probes and smoke tests: provide 3 probes with expected outputs and thresholds. Attach probe ids to ticket.
7) Playbook snippets: short triage steps for each alert type (one-sentence actions).

Metric definitions (compact reference):
- inference.request.count: count of API requests that reached serving runtime (label: route, model_version, tenant_id)
- inference.first_token.latency_ms: ms between request ingress and first token emitted (labels: route, model_version)
- inference.token.error_rate: fraction of requests resulting in model runtime error (labels: error_type)
- inference.kv.hit_rate: ratio kv_hits/(kv_hits+kv_misses) measured per model shard
- inference.kv.miss_latency_ms.p95: latency of kv misses (p95)
- routing.fallback.rate: percent of requests routed to fallback model variant

Tracing quick conventions for handoff:
- Minimal span set: request.received -> routing.decision -> model.decode_inputs -> runtime.generate_block -> runtime.kv_lookup -> response.sent
- Always attach correlation ids: request_id, session_id, canary_bucket
- Use the tag quantized=true/false to help filter perf regressions caused by quantization profiles
- For multi-model fanout, include parent_span for fanout controller and child_span per model to keep trace trees shallow

Dashboard notes and widget guidance (compact):
- Use 1m rollups for first 15 minutes post-rollout, then 5m for steady state
- For cost-aware panels show token-rate alongside GPU utilization to surface cost-per-token anomalies
- Keep example prompts (anonymized) in a single scroll widget to accelerate replay during triage
- For tenant-heavy rollouts, add a tenant top-talkers panel with sampled tenant traces (not full payloads)

Investigation playlist (triage flow):
1) Confirm alert root: metric spike vs sample traces.
2) Open top 3 slow traces and inspect span timings (is runtime.generate_block dominating?).
3) Check kv_hit_rate and eviction_count to spot cold-cache storms.
4) Verify routing.fallback.rate to see if traffic was shifted to slower variant.
5) If error_rate increased, fetch last 10 error traces and inspect error_type tag.
6) If nothing obvious, roll traffic to baseline and start capture of 100% traces for 2 minutes for deeper analysis.

Operational constraints and best practices:
- Sampling: enable adaptive sampling where errors and high-latency traces are sampled at 100% but healthy traces sampled at 1% to keep costs predictable.
- Privacy: redact user prompt text at the ingestion boundary; store only fingerprint or hash on dashboard panels used for triage.
- Widget budgets: keep each dashboard under 20 widgets initially; add deep-dive pages separately.

Mini-runbook to attach to release ticket (one-paragraph):
Attach this checklist + three dashboard URLs. Confirm owners are paged. Run synthetic probes for 5 minutes pre-rollout. Start canary at 5% for 15 minutes, escalate to 25% if no alerts, then gradual ramp. If any P1 fires, immediate rollback to previous model and capture trace bundle for postmortem.

Open questions for followup:
- What is the acceptable cost budget for 72h high-fidelity tracing per release? (prod finance + eng)
- Should we standardize a single probe template for all model rollouts?

Notes to self (for next iteration):
- Create a dashboard template generator that populates the compact kit from metric manifests.
- Add a short checklist card in Console UI that surfaces this handoff checklist when scheduling a canary.
